mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Corporate Registration (Corporate Registration Full Certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry Office of the Supreme Court of Korea, district registry in the jurisdiction of the registered office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path only. The registry certificate is notarized as required, then an Apostille is issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. Consular legalization is not used and must not be chained after the Apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Tax Clearance Certificate / Certificate of No Delinquent National Taxes)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: District Tax Office, National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path only for Korean-issued tax certificates. The certificate is sealed by the National Tax Service, and an Apostille is issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. Consular legalization is not applied.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Chusik Hoesa, evidenced before a Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path if executed in Korea: notarization before a Korean notary, then Apostille issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. If executed by a foreign shareholder in a non-Hague Contracting State, the alternative path is notarization under local law, authentication by the foreign state central foreign affairs authority, then Consular Legalization by the Embassy or Consulate of the Republic of Korea in that state. The two modes are parallel and mutually exclusive and must never be used sequentially on the same document.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry Office of the district court and the incorporating notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path only if the document originates in Korea or another Apostille Contracting State: notarization, then Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. For a non-Apostille state, the parallel and exclusive path is notarization, authentication by the local Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then Consular Legalization by the Republic of Korea Embassy or Consulate. Apostille and Consular Legalization are never chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: A licensed deposit-taking bank in the Republic of Korea where the corporate operating account will be maintained
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: the bank authorised signatory signs before a Korean notary, and the notarised signature is Apostilled by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. Consular Legalization applies only when the originating bank is in a non-Apostille state, and in that case the consular legalization is used alone, not after an Apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO and Senior Management Declaration for AML Customer Due Diligence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ultimate Beneficial Owners, representative director, and company secretary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: declaration executed before a Korean notary in the presence of each UBO, then Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. If executed at a Korean consulate in a non-Apostille state, the consular officer authentication constitutes the sole legalization; no Apostille is added.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every proposed shareholder, director, ultimate beneficial owner, authorised signatory and bank account signatory must be screened against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the FATF List of High-Risk Jurisdictions, the sanctions lists published by the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit, and the domestic KOFIU adverse media and PEP database. Politically Exposed Persons must be identified before incorporation, with automated adverse media alerts, source of wealth and source of funds verification, written senior management approval, enhanced ongoing monitoring for 12 months, and mandatory suspicious transaction reporting to the KOFIU for any unexplained high-value inflow. Screening results must be refreshed within 24 hours of signing the incorporation documents and on a continuous real-time basis, and any positive hit or unclear name match must suspend the incorporation process pending clearance from counsel.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (court registry portal operated by the Court Administration Office of the Supreme Court of Korea)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered name of the Chusik Hoesa must be in Hangeul script. Where a foreign-language corporate name is intended, it must be phonetically transliterated into Hangeul, and the Hangeul transliterated name controls the registry record. The name must follow a four-tier structure: (i) distinctive main brand or domain mark; (ii) descriptive business activity corresponding to ISIC 5820 and hyper-casual mobile game publishing; (iii) optional geographic or scale qualifier; and (iv) the legal form suffix Chusik Hoesa (Stock Corporation). Identical or misleadingly similar Hangeul names already registered in the national registry are rejected, and any concurrent English name must be supported by a certified romanisation table for bank and payment-rail onboarding.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation may be extended by filing a written extension request with the registry before expiry; extension is not automatic and requires a fresh search. On rejection, the applicant shall correct the prohibited, identical, or misleadingly similar element and refile through the same online registry portal. If the applicant believes the rejection is erroneous, counsel must submit a written objection to the registry officer within 14 days, attaching a legal memorandum demonstrating distinctiveness, including the four-tier name structure and transliteration table required by the registry. If the registry denies the objection, the applicant may file administrative litigation with the competent Administrative Court within 90 days of service of the denial; the registry decision stays in effect until a court orders re-registration.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A mere virtual-office mailbox or agent-only registered address will be rejected by the National Tax Service and by Korean AML-regulated banks in the AdMob and AppLovin payout flow, even though hyper-casual game publishing does not require a separate statutory licence. The company must demonstrate a fixed place of business for VAT registration under the Value-Added Tax Act and a genuine commercial subsistence under the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit CDD framework for corporate payment rails. A conditionally accepted virtual office must provide a dedicated serviced office, a Korean registered business address, actual lease or sublease with physical control, meeting room access, mail handling, and at least one locally employed officer in Korea. A pure commercial mailbox will not satisfy tax registration, bank onboarding, or overseas gaming advertising counterparty due diligence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced inspection: (1) actual office sign and ability to receive site visits; (2) lease contract, utility bills, and rent receipts; (3) payroll and personnel documents matching registry records; (4) game publishing records, ad revenue statements, and payment processor settlement reports; (5) board minutes and accounting records physically accessible at the registered office. Quantified risk for ISIC 5820 hyper-casual publisher: approximately 10% annual base probability of unannounced municipal tax or registry inspection for a low-risk entity. If one red flag is present, probability rises to 40%. If two or more red flags are present, such as a virtual mailbox and zero local employees, the probability exceeds 85%. Inspectors may coordinate across tax and registry authorities and may arrive on two hours notice.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Act No. 1001, as amended, particularly Articles 288 (formation requirements), 289 (articles of incorporation), 292 (subscription of shares), 293 (payment of shares), 295 (notarization), 299 (certification), and 317 (registration of incorporation); Foreign Investment Promotion Act for non-resident subscribers.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporate Registration Section, Civil Registration Division, District Court of the Republic of Korea where the registered office is located; online filings via the Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IRO).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Corporation (Chusik Hoesa) with notarized Articles of Incorporation and capital payment certificate attached.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Commercial Act does not require minimum paid-up capital for a Chusik Hoesa. However, the full par value of every subscribed share must be deposited into a Korean bank account before filing; a capital payment certificate must be obtained. No statutory blocked or escrowed account is required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, operating the HomeTax electronic portal (www.hometax.go.kr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Chusik Hoesa (Stock Corporation) domiciled in South Korea must register with the National Tax Service through the competent district tax office that has jurisdiction over its registered head office or domestic place of business. The registration application must be filed online via HomeTax or by paper submission within one month of the commencement of business. Required documents include the company's court registry certificate (corporate registration certificate), articles of incorporation, proof of foreign capital investment registration where applicable, lease agreement or other evidence of a fixed domestic place of business, identity documents and passports of the statutory directors/representative, and a power of attorney appointing a domestic tax representative if the actual representative resides outside Korea. The NTS validates the filing and issues a 10-digit Business Registration Number (TIN/VAT ID) electronically on HomeTax and as a physical Business Registration Certificate. This single number is used for corporate tax withholding, VAT, and customs-identity purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. South Korea does not provide a U.S.-style check-the-box election, and hybrid-mismatch elections are not recognised for indirect tax purposes. Separate statutory consolidation provisions exist for certain domestic corporate tax electives, but those do not alter the entity-level VAT or withholding classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) governed by the Value Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover-based registration exemption. Every economic activity involving the supply of goods or services in South Korea triggers mandatory VAT registration with the NTS. A simplified taxpayer compliance status applies to very small businesses with prior-year taxable turnover not exceeding KRW 80,000,000, but this status does not waive the mandatory registration requirement.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Korea mandates electronic tax invoicing for all business-to-business VAT transactions. Any VAT-supplying business must transmit electronic tax invoices to the NTS HomeTax central clearing system or via an approved EDI/ERP API gateway. Each transmitted invoice receives a machine-readable anti-fraud key code and digital identifier from the NTS, creating a real-time fiscal clearance trail. The tax invoice must be issued within statutory deadlines, generally no later than the 10th day of the month following the month of taxable supply, and transmitted to the NTS within one business day of issuance. For business-to-consumer sales, cash receipts are required. Non-compliance results in input VAT denial, additional penalties, and administrative fines.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to goods physically exported from Korea upon presentation of a valid customs export declaration. Qualifying offshore digital services, including mobile game software, subscription content, and remote gaming services supplied to non-resident users who consume the service outside Korea, also qualify for the zero rate under Article 21 of the Korean VAT Act. The service must be performed or deemed consumed outside Korea, the counterparty must not have a Korean tax nexus, and the consideration must be receivable in a foreign currency. For hyper-casual game export, monetisation through foreign advertising platforms may require the underlying invoice to be issued to a foreign advertiser or holding company to substantiate foreign-service treatment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service Export Declaration (Bill of Entry) evidencing the actual export of physical goods
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill or international courier receipt covering the exported consignment
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or Foreign Exchange Settlement Certificate issued by a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank
Commercial invoice matched to the customs declaration and foreign exchange proceeds
Foreign-level service agreement or purchase order identifying the non-resident recipient
Digital platform payout statements and app-store settlement reports for offshore digital game services and advertising revenues
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS strictly audits zero-rated claims by cross-referencing export declarations, foreign-currency receipt data, and underlying contracts. Unsupported or fraudulent zero-rating triggers reversal of the VAT refund, retrospective tax-bearing assessment, punitive interest, under-reporting penalties of up to 20% for negligence, fraud penalties of up to 40% of the undisclosed or unlawfully refunded amount, and criminal referral under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act. Clawback is not time-barred when tax evasion is demonstrated.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), acting jointly with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) as the statutory foreign-exchange policy authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA), with enforcement oversight by the Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) and transaction reporting captured through the Foreign Exchange Information Network (FEIN).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a market-determined, free-floating exchange rate for the Korean won regime in which current-account convertibility is genuinely open: software publishing, ad-monetized digital game services, and associate service fees generated from foreign advertising networks are treated as invisible trade earnings and may be collected freely in foreign currency. However, the regulatory scaffolding remains prescriptive. Every receipt of export proceeds must be routed into a domestic foreign-exchange bank (FX bank) and reported via FEIN with a suitable purpose code; there is no obligation to convert into won, but the original foreign currency must be hosted onshore unless creditable against approved payments. Capital-account operations, including non-resident equity injections, offshore loans, and dividend remittances to foreign shareholders, are more controlled by FETA prior-signal or reporting rules. Profit repatriation is lawful only after audited financial statements are finalized, corporate income tax is settled at 10%-25% statutory rates (treaty relief applied to non-residents), and the FX bank validates the dividend payment under a tax-completion certificate and inward remittance confirmation. Therefore the system is best characterized as current-account liberal, capital-account managed, and surveillance-intensive: the corporation enjoys full earning conversion flexibility, but every cross-border flow must be documentary and bank-intermediated, minimizing the risk of unnoticed offshore treasury leakage.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Article 15 of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Enforcement Decree, proceeds from digital-game service exports must be collected within 6 months from the service performance/invoice date; the counterpart foreign-exchange bank may grant extensions up to 12 months on demonstration of contractual payment terms. No mandatory conversion ratio exists, meaning the Chusik Hoesa may retain up to 100% of foreign-currency ad revenue in an onshore foreign-currency account, but the receipt must be reported through FEIN and matched to the applicable service-export purpose code with supporting e-tax invoices, publisher payout statements, and the export-contract archive.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: General corporate current account (KRW) plus foreign-currency demand deposit account and FX dealing line
Corporate settlement account (KRW) plus foreign-currency account and digital corporate onboarding package
Trade and overseas-remittance account, foreign-currency multi-currency account, and FX hedging credit line
Corporate deposit account plus foreign-currency demand deposit and advisory treasury services

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability as a primary treasury counterparty. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Airwallex, and Revolut Business do not hold a Korean banking license under the Banking Act nor a foreign-exchange dealer registration under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; therefore they cannot issue Korean-account-format KRW settlement facilities or represent a legal clearing rail for a resident Chusik Hoesa on standalone basis. They may be used only as supplementary wallet aggregators to receive USD/EUR AdMob or AppLovin payouts before sweeping into a licensed domestic foreign-exchange bank account, which remains mandatory for FEIN reporting, tax reconciliation, and capital controls. Domestic fintechs such as KakaoBank and Toss Bank offer genuine onshore corporate KRW accounts but their foreign-exchange and trade services are back-to-back delivered by licensed banks, thus providing no treasury advantage over the Tier-1 relationships and banning the EMI shortcut.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical in-branch appearance is mandatory at least once for the statutory representative director and first signatory to register the corporate seal card (인감카드) before any account activation; Tier-1 banks permit a fully remote digital onboarding process for resident directors using the corporate seal certificate, entity authentication under the Digital Signature Act, and an enforcement video call, but a foreign-currency account opening and any FX derivative line approval will normally trigger a second-level compliance video or in-person interview. Non-resident directors or beneficial owners are required to present certified passport copies, apostilled board resolutions, and either appear at a Korean branch or undergo consular notarization delegated to the bank’s overseas correspondent; in all cases the bank compliance committee retains discretion to demand a callback to the registered head office in South Korea.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity with multi-jurisdictional shareholders or nominee/foundation ownership blocking beneficial-ownership identification under the Real Name Financial Transactions Act and the Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate registry extract (법인등기부등본), business registration certificate (사업자등록증), complete shareholder ledger reaching the natural-person UBO, bank remittance confirmation evidencing the original source of the paid-in capital, notarized board resolution, apostilled UBO declarations, and a source-of-funds statement signed by the representative director.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Fragmenting high-volume AdMob/AppLovin ad payouts arriving from multiple Google and AppLovin legal entities (e.g., Google Ireland, Google Asia Pacific, AppLovin US) that resemble structured deposits or smurfing patterns in bank transaction monitoring.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed Google AdMob publisher agreement and AppLovin publisher agreement, 12 months of payout statements with payment identifiers, specification of Meta, TikTok, and Unity Ads user-acquisition campaigns, sample e-tax invoices (전자세금계산서) zero-rated for export, and a corporate treasury narrative describing the hyper-casual ad-monetization model and payout thresholds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: FEIN anomaly triggered by foreign-currency receipts landing beyond the statutory 6-month export-proceeds collection window, which banks escalate as suspected indirect export financing or unlicensed FX dealing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Ad-network remittance cycle schedules and invoice calendars, the foreign-exchange bank-approved extension certificate for foreign-currency collection, bank inward transfer confirmations (외화획득확인), the export sales tax-exemption report, and contractual payment terms proving the receivables schedule.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-to-banking reconciliation gap: annual corporate tax filings on digital-service export revenue do not match aggregate FEIN-reported FX receipts, prompting a suspicious transaction report under the Specified Financial Transaction Information Act.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate tax payment certificate (납세증명서), the latest corporate income tax return and audited financial statements, monthly FX receipt reconciliation keyed to FEIN report IDs and tax invoice numbers, VAT export-zero-rated schedule, and an independent Korean-licensed tax accountant (세무사) compliance conclusion letter.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident shareholders inject capital by wiring USD, EUR, or JPY into the domestic counterpart foreign-exchange bank’s designated subscription-money account using the Korea Standard Foreign Exchange Transactions purpose classification for acquisition of domestically-issued equity securities; the bank issues a certificate of capital payment (납입증명서) enabling the incorporation filings at the court registry. Within 30 days of share acquisition by a foreign investor, the acquirer must file a report under FETA through the counterpart FX bank to obtain a foreign-investment registration certificate (외국인투자신고필증) when the transaction exceeds the notifiable threshold. All inbound AdMob and AppLovin payouts arrive as SWIFT MT103 credits into a designated USD or EUR foreign-currency account maintained at the lead domestic bank, classified under the BPM6 services purpose code for computer and information services, supported by the dynamic publisher agreements. The treasury automatically initiates a spot KRW trade at the lead bank to cover local operating cash, with no surrender obligation; capital verification is evidenced by the bank payment confirmation and the FEIN report archive.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operating outflows for user acquisition (Meta Ads, TikTok Ads, Unity Ads, AppLovin DSP), analytics (Adjust, AppsFlyer), and cloud hosting settle predominantly by SWIFT MT103 open-account payments or commercial corporate cards initiated through the bank’s bulk payment platform; standard trade instruments such as commercial standby letters of credit and documentary collections (D/P, D/A) are reserved for physical media distribution or localized publishing agreements where a transport document exists. The treasury should maintain a single-collateral multi-currency pool (KRW, USD, EUR) at one lead bank to execute internal FX conversion at interbank spreads, automate KRW tax and payroll debits, and support monthly FEIN reconciliation, while keeping separate USD and EUR ledger sub-accounts to virtually align receivable currencies with the AdMob and AppLovin payout rails.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable KRW/USD FX forwards with maturity up to 12 months, permitted for hedging projected AdMob/AppLovin ad-revenue receivables up to 100% of forecast exposure evidenced by contracts and payout statements, subject to the FX bank’s credit line and FEIN reporting.
KRW/USD FX swaps for short-term liquidity rebalancing between the foreign-currency payout account and the KRW operating account, conducted only with the licensed domestic foreign-exchange bank.
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCS) restricted to balance-sheet hedging of any future foreign-currency borrowings or bond proceeds, prohibited for speculative mismatch positions.

FX options including zero-cost collars and premium-bearing KRW/USD puts or calls for hedging the anticipated annual USD ad-revenue stream with option expiry no longer than one year and underlying documentation.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are largely non-desirable for onshore Korean corporate: the KRW has a deliverable onshore market, and a resident entity can access NDF only through a licensed FX bank with strict documentary proof of an underlying foreign-currency debt or trade obligation; uncovered exploratory NDF positions violate FETA and are therefore not part of the treasury blueprint.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return and annual tax payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of Korea (NTS) through the local district tax office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end; for a December 31 year-end, no later than March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under the Framework Act on National Taxes, failure to file attracts an additional tax of 20% of the unpaid tax amount; understatement in a filed return attracts 10% of the understated tax amount; overdue tax accrues interest at 0.022% per day (approximately 8.03% per annum) from the statutory due date to the actual payment date. Prolonged non-payment and non-filing can lead to tax seizure and administrative closure of the business registration, followed by cancellation of the corporate business license.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Income Tax Surtax Return and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government tax authority of the jurisdiction where the head office is located (metropolitan city or provincial tax administration), filed through the National Tax Service or local tax e-filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the last day of the month following the corporate income tax return deadline; for a December 31 year-end, no later than April 30 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under the Local Tax Act, non-filing and underreporting are subject to local income tax additional taxes of 10% and 20% respectively, plus daily overdue interest of 0.022% for late payment; the local government may request compulsory collection through the National Tax Service and may administratively close the business registration for chronic delinquency.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ordinary General Meeting of Shareholders and approval of the annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No government filing is made; the meeting is conducted internally in accordance with the Korean Commercial Act at the registered head office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year; for a December 31 year-end, the AGM must be held no later than March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the AGM or to obtain shareholder approval of the financial statements constitutes a breach of the Korean Commercial Act; directors are liable to shareholders and creditors for resulting losses, and the act provides for a non-compliance fine against responsible directors of up to KRW 5,000,000. Repeated deadlock or failure of corporate governance can in extreme cases support a court-ordered dissolution petition.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External Audit Report and audited financial statements (mandatory only when statutory audit thresholds are met)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through the DART electronic disclosure system, where disclosure is required; the audit report is also delivered to shareholders before the AGM
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a December 31 fiscal year-end, the independent CPA audit must be completed and the auditor's report delivered in time for the AGM to approve the audited financial statements by March 31; filings required under the External Audit Act are submitted to the FSS through DART without delay after the AGM and in no event later than 14 days after AGM approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, failure to obtain and disclose a statutory audit report can result in administrative fines of up to KRW 50,000,000, referral to the Securities and Futures Commission, invalidity of the unaudited financial statements for shareholder approval, and director liability for damages caused to shareholders or creditors.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Annual Business Report (only if the Chusik Hoesa qualifies as a foreign-invested company under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) / Invest Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the end of the fiscal year; for a December 31 year-end, no later than March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, failure to submit the annual foreign investment business report attracts an administrative fine of up to KRW 2,000,000 per case, and may jeopardize foreign-investment protection, foreign-invested company registration status, and any applicable tax exemptions or incentives.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, etc. and the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act, an independent certified CPA audit is mandatory for: (i) any company listed or publicly traded on a Korean securities market, regardless of asset size; (ii) any financial company; (iii) any unlisted stock company, including a Chusik Hoesa, whose total assets at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year are KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9 million) or more; and (iv) any company designated by the Securities and Futures Commission for public-interest reasons. For ordinary privately held game-publishing companies, the only routine quantitative balance-sheet trigger is the KRW 12 billion total-assets threshold; Korea does not impose a standalone turnover or headcount audit trigger for non-listed private stock companies. Additional mandatory audit requirements may arise for consolidated reporting groups and for companies claiming certain tax incentives or regulatory approvals when the competent authority requires CPA-certified financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Listed companies and companies required to do so apply Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS); unlisted private companies not required to adopt K-IFRS may apply Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP) under the business accounting standards for non-public companies. Independent audits are performed in accordance with Korean Standards on Auditing (KSA), which are aligned with the International Standards on Auditing.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korea does not require a standalone annual UBO declaration form for a non-financial private Chusik Hoesa. However, the shareholder register is a mandatory statutory book that must be continuously maintained, and a share transfer is effective against the company and third parties only when the transferee is entered in the register. For a foreign-invested Korean company, any transfer, pledge, or change in ownership that changes the foreign investor or beneficial owner must be reported to MOTIE through KOTRA within 30 days from the date of the change. As a matter of corporate secretarial good practice, an annual reconciliation of the shareholder register, share transfer records, UBO information, and AGM attendance list should be completed before the annual shareholders' meeting; failure to update the register can result in loss of owner rights and administrative fines under applicable statutes.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (shareholder register) kept at the head office
Register of Directors (board member register) kept at the head office
Register of Statutory Auditors and Audit Committee members, if any
Register of Charges, Mortgages, and encumbrances over company assets, if any
Minute Book of shareholders' meetings and board of directors' meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 to USD 1,500 per year for a licensed corporate service provider, registered office, and company secretarial support in Seoul; the range increases to USD 1,500 to USD 3,500 if full AGM preparation, register maintenance, and UBO/share transfer monitoring are outsourced
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 to USD 20,000 for a certified CPA audit of a privately held Chusik Hoesa under Korean Standards on Auditing, depending on total assets, transaction volume, intercompany balances, and monetization revenue from hyper-casual gaming operations

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% top marginal corporate income tax rate; progressive statutory rates of 9%, 19%, 21% and 24% on the corporate tax base under the Korean Corporate Income Tax Act
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory patent box or preferential free-zone rate is available for hyper-casual mobile game publishing; limited tax incentives apply through R&D expenditure tax credits (up to 30-50% of eligible R&D costs for SMEs/DLT under the Special Tax Reduction Control Act), foreign investment zone incentives for qualifying FDI, and small/medium enterprise (SME) income deductions. No general tax holiday for gaming royalties or AdMob/AppLovin advertising revenue.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return (Form No. 60, '법인세 과세표준 및 세액신고서') filed electronically via the Korean National Tax Service HomeTax portal (www.hometax.go.kr); accompanying Schedule 10 (Non-Resident Income) and Form 51 (Tax Treaty Exemption/Reduction Request) for non-resident taxpayers
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the end of each fiscal year under Article 60(1) of the Corporate Income Tax Act; for a December 31 year-end, the filing deadline is March 31 of the following year (next business day if March 31 falls on a non-business day). Non-resident corporations without a permanent establishment must file the same annual return for Korean-source income by the same 3-month deadline through their Korean withholding agent or tax representative.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Entity identification, business registration number, head office location, fiscal year, and legal form
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Chusik Hoesa registration number and Korean address. Where the direct/copyright owner is foreign, attach the Non-Resident Business Registration Form and state the name and tax residence of the ultimate beneficial owner to avoid being classified as a transparent intermediary.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Classification of income: Korean-source versus foreign-source income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Korean-source income derived from hyper-casual game publishing unless a permanent establishment exists. AdMob/AppLovin payouts sourced from Korean users constitute taxable Korean-source service/royalty income; accurately bifurcate domestic ad revenue from offshore platform settlement fees.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue, sales, platform commissions, and digital advertising revenue
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the full gross gaming revenue from ad networks before platform commissions; do not net out AdMob/AppLovin fees. Cross-border contract allocation must comply with OECD transfer pricing principles; any unbalanced cost-plus arrangement will be adjusted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of sales, operating expenses, deductions, and allowable bad debts
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct royalties, server costs, engineering wages, and user-acquisition costs only with proper invoices and evidence of benefit. Payments to related offshore marketing companies are disallowed if the services lack economic substance or cannot be documented.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income / taxable income before loss carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile statutory accounting net income to tax base using Schedule 6 (tax adjustments). Non-resident shareholders must avoid using foreign shipping or royalty deductions unrelated to the Korean digital game business.

Claim only NOLs arising within the statutory 10-year carryforward period. Restrict the deduction to the Korean-source business activity; a foreign branch or shell entity's foreign losses cannot offset Korean game income.

Enter the net Korean taxable base. If a permanent establishment exists, calculate Korean-source taxable income under domestic accounting rules; if no permanent establishment exists, the base is the separate withholding tax base for dividends, royalties, and interest only.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax computed at progressive rates (9%, 19%, 21%, 24%)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the four bracket rates to the tax base. For a non-resident enterprise, the withholding tax rates may reduce or replace the normal corporate tax if the income is not effectively connected with a Korean permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits: foreign tax credit, R&D credit, temporary investment credit, employment credit
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim foreign tax credit for withholding taxes imposed on AdMob/AppLovin remittances. A Korean Chusik Hoesa cannot claim foreign tax credit for taxes paid by a transparent offshore sister entity; provide Form 1025 and bank receipts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total corporate tax due plus local income tax surcharge
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Local income tax is an additional 10% of the corporate tax amount (effectively 22% combined on non-resident distributions). For non-resident payees with treaty relief, attach Form 51 and the foreign Tax Residency Certificate before the return is filed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-resident dividend/interest/royalty withholding tax reconciliation and DTA relief schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List all outbound remittances of dividends, royalties, or interest. Indicate treaty-eligible items separately and substantiate beneficial ownership. Failing to attach the Treaty Application Form disqualifies the reduced rate and may trigger a 40% fraudulent underreporting penalty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior year tax return adjustments, provisional tax prepayments, audit adjustments, and additional tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include any previous year adjustments discovered by the Korean tax office. Late prepayments are enforced with monthly delinquency surcharges of 1.2% (maximum 72% of deficient tax); directors consenting to false declarations are criminally exposed.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing under the Framework Act on National Taxes attracts a 20% unfaithful-return penalty (Article 47-3), a 10% understatement penalty for non-fraud cases, a 40% penalty for fraudulent understatement (Article 47-4), plus monthly delinquency interest of 1.2% capped at 72% of the unpaid tax. Criminal evasion under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act carries imprisonment of up to 2 years, up to 5 years for repeated or aggravated evasion, and fines up to twice the evaded tax plus civil restitution.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% statutory withholding tax on outbound dividends payable to non-resident shareholders, plus a 2% local income tax surcharge (22% combined effective withholding rate). Under an applicable bilateral DTA, this may be reduced (commonly to 5% for >10% shareholding and 10%-15% otherwise).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the Korean withholding agent must retain the dividend, interest, or royalty payment at the domestic rate and then the beneficial owner must submit to the Korean National Tax Service: (i) a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the relevant foreign tax authority; (ii) a completed 'Application for Non-Resident Income Withholding Tax Exemption/Reduction' (Form 51) or equivalent; (iii) documentation proving beneficial ownership and absence of a conduit/back-to-back transaction; and (iv) reasonable evidence of Korean-source character and relation to the game publishing royalty contract. An advance treaty ruling or prior-year refund claim may also be filed within the statutory statute-of-limitations period; no treaty relief is granted to a nominee receiving the income on behalf of a resident shareholder.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on royalties and interest is also 20% plus 2% local income tax (22% combined); most comprehensive DTA protocols reduce interest and royalty withholding to between 10% and 15% when the beneficial owner is a qualified treaty resident. For hyper-casual game IP royalties, the taxpayer must prove that the technology or copyright is genuinely owned by the foreign beneficiary and that no steel-tax avoidance structure exists under Article 6 of the International Tax Adjustment Act.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Under Article 6 of the International Tax Adjustment Act, mandatory Local File and Master File documentation is required when the Korean Chusik Hoesa's international related-party transaction amount exceeds KRW 5 billion during the fiscal year; the Master File is separately required when annual revenue exceeds KRW 100 billion and related-party transactions exceed KRW 5 billion. The documentation must be filed within 6 months after the fiscal year-end and contemporaneous with the tax return.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not apply the UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR), but substance is enforced through the General Anti-Avoidance Rule, the 'actual place of effective management' test under the Corporate Income Tax Act, and the OECD Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) standard. A hyper-casual game publisher must show Korean-based employees performing game operations, ad monetization strategy, risk management, and strategic decision-making; having only a registered office with nominal share capital and no local activity will cause the Korean tax authorities to recharacterize the Chusik Hoesa as a shell or thin-capitalized intermediary.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Revenue Suppression via Offshore Nominee Accounts
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Underreporting AdMob/AppLovin ad-monetization revenue while directing substantial gross receipts to a related Hong Kong or BVI company disguised as 'marketing services' or 'game marketing expense', without any substantive service being performed, in order to avoid Korean corporate income tax and dividend withholding tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Articles 3 and 8 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, willful tax evasion is punishable by imprisonment of up to 2 years (up to 5 years for aggravated repeated violations) or a fine not exceeding the evaded tax; the Korean NTS additionally imposes a 40% fraudulent understatement penalty under the Framework Act on National Taxes Article 47-4, plus delinquency surcharges of up to 72% of the unpaid amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Representative directors who sign falsified returns are not shielded by the corporate veil; under Article 399 of the Korean Commercial Act they are jointly and severally liable to compensate the company for tax losses caused by intentional misfeasance, and the NTS can attach directors' personal assets, impose a departure (travel) ban via the National Tax Collection Act, and bring criminal charges leading to imprisonment; directors of the funnel entity are also personally exposed to criminal fines and civil recovery of converted AdMob/AppLovin payouts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Disguised Dividend Repatriation and Thin Capitalization Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Recharacterizing an outbound dividend from the Chusik Hoesa to the foreign shareholder as an interest or royalty payment on inflated intercompany loans or intangible licenses, particularly where the foreign shareholder loan exceeds a debt-to-equity ratio of 3:1 and no genuine service or funding risk exists in the Korean entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 15-2 of the International Tax Adjustment Act disallows interest deductions on excessive owner loans; the offending payment is recharacterized as a deemed dividend subject to 22% Korean withholding tax plus understatement penalties and interest; false invoices for royalties or interest may trigger the punitive 40% fraudulent-filing penalty; the tax authority may also apply the anti-avoidance rule to retroactively deny treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly execute bogus loan documents or licensing contracts face personal joint liability for the deficient taxes; willful deception can result in asset seizure, travel blacklisting, and imprisonment for up to 5 years under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act. Because the corporate form is pierced where the loan structure has no independent arm's-length economic purpose, the foreign shareholder and Korean directors are jointly responsible for all restored profits and criminal restitution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Economic Substance Failure and Transfer Pricing Misallocation of Intangibles
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the hyper-casual game publishing business as a Korean shell that holds no employees, no operating authority, and no risk management function, while assigning the high-value game IP and all user-advertising revenue to a zero-tax offshore subsidiary at cost without paying an arm's-length profit split under a TNMM or profit-split methodology.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Korean NTS will invoke Article 6 of the International Tax Adjustment Act to reallocate the profits to the Korean Chusik Hoesa, applying the arm's length principle and assessing the full corporate income tax differential plus a 10% unfaithful-return penalty (40% for fraud), daily delinquency surcharges, and local income tax surcharge; illegal tax avoidance acts may be criminally prosecuted under Article 3-6 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Where the offshore structure fails economic substance, the domestic directors are treated as having actively participated in the artificial disposal of assets; the Korean NTS will pierce the corporate veil to collect unpaid taxes from their personal estates, issue travel bans and asset attachment, and refer the case for prosecution. Directors may receive imprisonment terms of up to 5 years and fines equal to three times the tax evaded, in addition to permanent disqualification from serving as Korean company directors.
